name: FLORES-101
description: FLORES-101 is an evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and professionally translated into 101 languages. The sentences cover a variety of topics and domains, sourced from Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage. All translations are multilingually aligned, enabling evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems across 10,100 language pairs.
creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan (Facebook AI Research, LORIA)
inLanguage: 101 languages including English, Spanish, French, German, Chinese, Arabic, Hindi, and 94 others
citeAs: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan. 2021. The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation. arXiv:2106.03193v1 [cs.CL]
rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia sources including Wikinews (international news articles), Wikijunior (age-appropriate nonfiction books for children), and WikiVoyage (travel guides). The selection process involved randomly selecting articles from each source and manually selecting 3-5 contiguous sentences from each article. Paragraphs were sampled equally from the beginning, middle, and end of articles. The selection was performed by 10 annotators from the research lab with diverse backgrounds (6 male, 4 female; researchers and program/project managers; from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America).
rai:dataCollectionRawData: All source sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia, specifically from Wikinews (one third), Wikijunior (one third), and WikiVoyage (one third). These are public and freely available repositories under permissive licensing covering a broad range of topics.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences. Paragraphs were selected from the beginning, middle, or end of articles, balanced to be equally distributed across the corpus. For each sentence, metadata was extracted including Wikipedia URL, topic, and boolean flags indicating whether the sentence contained entities linked to other Wikipedia pages and images. All sentences were manually labeled by sub-topic (one of 10 possibilities: crime, disasters, entertainment, geography, health, nature, politics, science, sports, and travel).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentences were professionally translated by Language Service Providers (LSPs) through a carefully controlled process. The workflow included: (1) translation and editing by an initial LSP, (2) automated quality control checks (language identification, copy detection from commercial translation engines, length verification, fluency checking), (3) quality assurance by an independent LSP providing a translation quality score (0-100 scale) based on identified errors (grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, register), and (4) re-translation if the quality score was below 90%. Translations with more than 10% of sentences violating automatic checks were re-translated prior to human evaluation. The process was iterative, with translations potentially going through multiple rounds of re-translation based on quality assessment.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was assessed through a Translation Quality Score (0-100 scale) determined by the number and severity of identified errors. Errors were categorized by type (grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, register) and severity level (minor, major, critical). The acceptable translation quality score threshold was set at 90%. The largest error category across all languages was mistranslation. Evaluators paid particular attention to unnatural translation errors.
rai:annotatorDemographics: The sentence selection was performed by 10 annotators from the research lab: 6 male and 4 female, with different roles (researchers including scientists and engineers, and program/project managers), originally from different regions of the world (East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automated quality control checks were implemented including: language identification, checking whether translation is a copy of source sentence, checking for significant length differences, checking translation fluency according to a language model, and checking whether translation is a copy of translations from publicly available translation engines using sentence-level SentencePiece BLEU (spBLEU) with specific thresholds.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to foster progress in machine translation for low-resource languages, which would benefit the majority of the world's population who speak low-resource languages. By providing high-quality evaluation benchmarks for 101 languages including many low-resource languages, the dataset enables better assessment of model quality on the long tail of low-resource languages and supports development of many-to-many multilingual translation systems.
rai:dataBiases: All source sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia, meaning that source sentences not in English are produced by human translators, which introduces translationese (overly literal or awkward translations) with known idiosyncrasies. The authors conjecture these effects are marginal when evaluating models in low-resource languages where current MT systems produce many severe mistakes, and believe the benefits of many-to-many evaluation outweigh the risk of evaluating translationese.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to evaluation purposes with 3001 sentences, which may not be sufficient for training purposes. All source sentences originate from English Wikipedia, which may not represent all domains or cultural contexts. While the dataset covers 101 languages, several low-resource languages have relatively few articles in Wikipedia containing well-structured sentences. Translation quality varies across languages, with some languages near the 90% quality threshold. Performance analysis shows that translation between low-resource languages works poorly, with spBLEU scores below 5 points for many African language families (Bantu, Dravidian, Indo-Aryan, Nilotic). The dataset does not support all possible language pairs equally well, as performance is heavily correlated with the amount of training data available for each language.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluation of machine translation systems, particularly for low-resource and multilingual machine translation. It supports evaluation of many-to-many multilingual models across 10,100 language pairs. The dataset is divided into three splits: dev (997 sentences from 281 articles) for hyper-parameter tuning, devtest (1012 sentences from 281 articles) for testing during development phase, and test (992 sentences from 280 articles) available via evaluation server. Beyond machine translation, the dataset can be used to evaluate tasks such as document-level translation (due to contiguous sentences from same articles), multimodal translation (via image metadata), sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation. The test set is available only through a publicly available evaluation server to guarantee equivalent assessment of models and reduce overfitting.
